title: Third Word Worships Spiritual Lightness And Beliefs Security

questions.question: In the comparison, what do the two travelers stand for?
questions.answer: One stands for people who obey Allah’s law, and the other stands for people who rebel and follow their desires.

questions.question: What does the road represent in the passage?
questions.answer: It represents human life, beginning from the world of spirits, passing through the grave, and continuing to the hereafter.

questions.question: In this part of the comparison, what do the kit-bag and rifle symbolize?
questions.answer: They symbolize worship and fear of Allah.

questions.question: Why does worship seem heavy at first, yet become easy in reality?
questions.answer: Outwardly it looks like a burden, but inwardly it gives deep ease, relief, and strength.

questions.question: What belief is affirmed in the prayer mentioned here?
questions.answer: It is the testimony that no one is worthy of worship except Allah.

questions.question: How does this testimony change the way a worshipper sees the world?
questions.answer: He sees every created thing as pointing him to Allah’s mercy and care.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does the worshipper understand about who creates, provides, and controls harm and benefit?
questions.answer: He understands that all of that belongs to Allah alone.

questions.question: What does the worshipper do after recognizing Allah’s mercy and wisdom?
questions.answer: He turns to Allah in supplication, seeks refuge in Him, trusts Him, and relies on Him.

questions.question: What protection does belief give the worshipper?
questions.answer: It gives him firmness against disasters and fills him with confidence.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the root of courage?
questions.answer: True courage comes from belief in Allah and worship.

questions.question: What is the root of cowardice in the passage?
questions.answer: It comes from misguidance.

questions.question: What example is given to show the fearlessness of a heart brightened by worship?
questions.answer: Even if the whole earth were to explode, such a person would not panic but would view it with amazement at Allah’s power.

questions.question: What contrast is made with the philosopher?
questions.answer: Although he was thought to be intellectually advanced, his heart was empty, so he became frightened by a comet.

questions.question: What does the passage say about human ability and human needs?
questions.answer: Human needs are countless, but human resources and strength are very limited.

questions.question: How far do human hopes and fears reach compared to human power?
questions.answer: Human power reaches only a little, but hopes, desires, pains, and fears stretch very far.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from human weakness and need?
questions.answer: Worship, affirming Allah’s oneness, trusting Him, and submitting to Him are a great gain and blessing for the human soul.

questions.question: Which two human paths are being compared through the image of the two travelers?
questions.answer: The path of submission to divine guidance and the path of rebellion driven by personal desire.

questions.question: How is the journey of life described in relation to the grave and the hereafter?
questions.answer: Life is presented as a road that passes through the grave and continues into the next world.

questions.question: What two religious qualities are pictured as travel equipment and weaponry?
questions.answer: Worship and reverent fear of Allah.

questions.question: Why is the burden of worship called only apparent?
questions.answer: Because what looks difficult on the outside brings inward ease, peace, and support.

questions.question: In the prayer, what central truth does the worshipper testify to?
questions.answer: That only Allah is truly divine.

questions.question: How does this faith help the worshipper interpret all things around him?
questions.answer: He sees them as openings to Allah’s mercy rather than as random or independent forces.

questions.question: What does the worshipper believe about provision and control over events?
questions.answer: He believes Allah alone provides, creates, and governs benefit and harm.

questions.question: Why is Allah’s wisdom important in this passage?
questions.answer: It means nothing Allah does is meaningless or pointless.

questions.question: How does the worshipper respond once he realizes all things are under Allah’s command?
questions.answer: He seeks Allah’s protection and places his trust in Him.

questions.question: What emotional result comes from that trust?
questions.answer: It gives strong confidence and security.

questions.question: How are courage and belief connected here?
questions.answer: Real bravery grows out of faith and worship.

questions.question: How are cowardice and error connected here?
questions.answer: Fearfulness grows out of spiritual deviation.

questions.question: What extreme image is used to describe the boldness of a sincere worshipper?
questions.answer: He would stay calm even before a world-shaking explosion.

questions.question: Why is the philosopher used as a contrasting example?
questions.answer: To show that mental sharpness without a living heart can still leave a person weak and terrified.

questions.question: What imbalance in human life does the passage highlight?
questions.answer: People face endless needs and troubles, but they possess very little power and wealth of their own.

questions.question: Based on that imbalance, why are reliance and submission so important?
questions.answer: Because they connect weak human beings to the One who has complete power, mercy, and control.

questions.question: What kind of people does the first traveler represent in this passage?
questions.answer: People who live in obedience to Allah’s revealed law.

questions.question: What kind of people does the second traveler represent?
questions.answer: People who resist guidance and follow their lower desires.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the travel gear in the comparison?
questions.answer: It stands for worship and being conscious of Allah.

questions.question: What important paradox about worship does the passage teach?
questions.answer: It may look hard from the outside, but in its inner truth it brings comfort and lightness.

questions.question: What statement in prayer becomes the key to that comfort?
questions.answer: The declaration that there is no deity except Allah.

questions.question: How does this declaration affect the worshipper’s understanding of creation?
questions.answer: It teaches him that everything points back to Allah as the only true source and controller.

questions.question: What does the worshipper realize about suffering and blessing?
questions.answer: He realizes both are under Allah’s control, not in the hands of creation itself.

questions.question: How do wisdom and mercy together shape the worshipper’s view of Allah’s actions?
questions.answer: He understands that Allah’s actions are purposeful and filled with compassion.

questions.question: After reaching this understanding, what actions of the heart follow?
questions.answer: He makes du‘a, seeks shelter in Allah, trusts Him, and depends on Him.

questions.question: What practical result does this trust have when trouble comes?
questions.answer: It strengthens him against calamities.

questions.question: What inner quality does belief produce according to the passage?
questions.answer: It produces courage.

questions.question: What inner quality does misguidance produce?
questions.answer: It produces cowardice.

questions.question: How does the passage challenge the idea that intellectual fame guarantees real strength?
questions.answer: It shows that a celebrated thinker may still panic if he lacks spiritual grounding.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the limits of human control?
questions.answer: A person’s actual power reaches only a short distance and cannot match the size of his needs and fears.

questions.question: What four things are finally presented as a great blessing for the human spirit?
questions.answer: Worship, affirming Allah’s oneness, trusting Him, and surrendering to Him.

questions.question: What is the main contrast between the two symbolic travelers?
questions.answer: One follows Allah’s law, while the other follows his own rebellious impulses.

questions.question: What does the path itself symbolize beyond ordinary travel?
questions.answer: It symbolizes the full human journey from origin to the next life.

questions.question: Why are worship and fear of Allah compared to equipment carried on the road?
questions.answer: Because they help the believer travel safely and face what lies ahead.

questions.question: How does the passage correct the idea that worship only weighs a person down?
questions.answer: It explains that worship carries hidden relief and support that are greater than its outward demands.

questions.question: What is the spiritual importance of saying that none is worthy of worship except Allah?
questions.answer: It anchors the heart in Allah alone and opens the person to Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: How does that belief affect a person’s view of daily events and created things?
questions.answer: He sees them as connected to Allah’s care, not as independent powers.

questions.question: What does the passage say about who truly controls provision, harm, and benefit?
questions.answer: Allah alone controls them.

questions.question: Why does recognizing Allah’s authority over all things lead to prayer and trust?
questions.answer: Because once a person knows everything is under Allah’s rule, turning to Him becomes the natural response.

questions.question: What kind of security comes from relying on Allah?
questions.answer: A deep inner steadiness in the face of disasters.

questions.question: What moral lesson is given about bravery?
questions.answer: Real bravery grows from faith and worship.

questions.question: What moral lesson is given about fearfulness?
questions.answer: Deep fearfulness grows from spiritual error and distance from guidance.

questions.question: Why is the image of the earth exploding used?
questions.answer: To show how strong a believing heart can become when it truly trusts Allah.

questions.question: What weakness is exposed in the example of the philosopher?
questions.answer: Sharp reasoning without faith and a living heart can still leave a person helpless before fear.

questions.question: What two facts about human nature make reliance on Allah necessary?
questions.answer: Human beings have endless needs and troubles, but very little strength and ownership.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the reach of human wishes and worries?
questions.answer: They extend far beyond the small range of human ability.

questions.question: What overall judgment does the passage make about worship and trust in Allah?
questions.answer: They are a major source of profit, joy, and blessing for weak human beings.

questions.question: In this section, what does submission to divine law mean in contrast to following desire?
questions.answer: It means living by Allah’s guidance instead of making the self’s impulses the authority.

questions.question: How is human life pictured as a journey?
questions.answer: It is shown as a continuing road that moves through this life, the grave, and the life to come.

questions.question: What is represented by the carried items in the comparison?
questions.answer: They represent worship and fear of Allah.

questions.question: What mistaken impression about worship does the passage address?
questions.answer: The mistaken impression is that worship is only a hardship.

questions.question: What hidden benefit of worship is emphasized instead?
questions.answer: It gives inward relief, strength, and lightness.

questions.question: What truth does the worshipper speak in prayer?
questions.answer: He affirms Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: How does affirming Allah’s oneness help the worshipper deal with the world?
questions.answer: It helps him read the world through Allah’s mercy, wisdom, and care.

questions.question: What does the worshipper believe about Allah’s actions?
questions.answer: He believes Allah acts with wisdom and never without purpose.

questions.question: How does the worshipper view Allah’s mercy and generosity?
questions.answer: He sees them as abundant and always available.

questions.question: What does he do because of that view of Allah?
questions.answer: He calls upon Allah, seeks protection from Him, and trusts Him fully.

questions.question: What does this trust do for a believer in times of danger?
questions.answer: It strengthens him and guards him from collapsing inwardly.

questions.question: What source of courage is identified in the passage?
questions.answer: Faith joined with worship.

questions.question: What source of cowardice is identified in the passage?
questions.answer: Straying from truth.

questions.question: What is the point of comparing a sincere worshipper with a worldly philosopher?
questions.answer: The point is that spiritual faith can give more courage than bare intellectual reputation.

questions.question: Why does the passage stress that man needs many things but possesses almost nothing?
questions.answer: To show that human beings are too weak on their own and therefore need Allah constantly.

questions.question: According to the ending of the passage, what brings real benefit to the human spirit?
questions.answer: Worship, belief in Allah’s oneness, reliance on Him, and submission to Him.

questions.question: Who are symbolized by the obedient traveler and the rebellious traveler?
questions.answer: The obedient one symbolizes those who live under divine guidance, and the rebellious one symbolizes those who follow selfish desire.

questions.question: What larger reality is symbolized by the road?
questions.answer: The full course of human existence leading into the hereafter.

questions.question: What do the travel provisions and weapon stand for spiritually?
questions.answer: They stand for worship and fearing Allah with reverence.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the relationship between the outer form of worship and its inner meaning?
questions.answer: Its outer form may seem weighty, but its inner meaning gives extraordinary ease.

questions.question: Which statement made in prayer is central to this section?
questions.answer: The witness that there is no god but Allah.

questions.question: What door does this faith open for the worshipper, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It opens for him the way to Allah’s mercy in everything he encounters.

questions.question: What does the worshipper believe about who gives provision and who controls outcomes?
questions.answer: He believes Allah alone provides and controls all benefit and harm.

questions.question: How do Allah’s wisdom and compassion affect the worshipper’s confidence?
questions.answer: They assure him that Allah’s acts are meaningful and merciful, so he can trust Him.

questions.question: What four responses flow from that confidence?
questions.answer: Supplication, seeking refuge, trusting, and relying.

questions.question: What is the result of these responses when facing hardships?
questions.answer: The believer becomes inwardly protected and confident.

questions.question: What connection does the passage make between worship and bravery?
questions.answer: Worship rooted in belief gives rise to bravery.

questions.question: What connection does it make between misguidance and fear?
questions.answer: Misguidance produces fear and weakness.

questions.question: How does the example of the possible destruction of the earth highlight faith?
questions.answer: It shows that a heart lit by faith can remain calm even before something overwhelming.

questions.question: What does the philosopher’s panic reveal?
questions.answer: It reveals that a mind without spiritual depth can be shaken badly by fear.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the range of human power with the range of human hopes and troubles?
questions.answer: Human power is very limited, while hopes and troubles stretch far beyond that limit.

questions.question: What final insight should a reader draw about the human condition?
questions.answer: Since people are weak and needy, their true good lies in worshipping Allah, affirming His oneness, trusting Him, and submitting to Him.
